modes.vengeful: Banished at Ravenloft. He hunts: husks and omens cluster around whoever struck the final blow; offers come only as sneers.
modes.indebted/curious: Spared. He watches with something like professional interest and offers fair-seeming trades. He keeps his word — exactly.
modes.claimant: Bargained with, or Thorgrinn walked the Black Road. He considers something already his and arrives to inspect it.
modes.unset: No final choice was recorded. Treat as indebted/curious.

modes.vengeful: Banished. It wants the party bound and drained. It lays debts aggressively and turns rescued creditors against them.
modes.obsessed: Allowed to withdraw. It is fixated on one PC (default: Thorgrinn; Damien if he bargained) and courts them with gifts that are never free.
modes.possessive claimant: Bargained with. It holds a mark on someone and calls it in at the worst moment: a debt due during Last Bastion.
modes.unset: No final choice was recorded. Treat as obsessed (Thorgrinn).

modes.distant: He departed Barovia first and simply watches. Use only signs and one whisper per chapter.
modes.curious: Something in the finale fascinated him. One offer per chapter, always fair, always priced.
modes.claimant: He granted the Borrowed Ending, or holds a lesser deal. The price is live: see the Borrowed Ending item.

thresholds: Signs only (roll the omens table when a scene needs atmosphere). No offers.
One Shadow beat per session from the session guide. One Dark Gift may be offered per chapter. The power's signature rule is active.
Use the Shadow beat in every session. Offers can arrive in combat. The power's second signature clause is active. It names a price out loud before Last Bastion.

An echo of the power is physically present at the climax (8.3) — a voice, a shape in the steam, a hand on the regulator. It never replaces Korga, Hadrik or the Bastion Engine as the opponent. It sets the terms of the epilogue.

orcus.name: The Count of the Dying
orcus.offer: Orcus speaks the number of the dead if Last Bastion runs — then, slowly, the names. Lowhearth's names.
orcus.effect: Reveals R3 as knowledge: the party knows Lowhearth floods and where to find proof (Runa's bypass sheets, the Heartworks plates). It is not evidence.
orcus.price: +2 Orcus. The asker gains the Death-Mark of the Black Road.

orcus.name: Death, Denied
orcus.offer: One person who died in this arc rises at dawn, whole, with a cold soul.
orcus.effect: Returns one dead NPC to life without components (a worker, Tovik, a soldier — even Baldrik).
orcus.price: +3 Orcus. The returned person carries the Death-Mark. Orcus takes 'a death of equal weight' later: one Last Bastion pressure stage starts one step worse.

orcus.name: The Rider's Night (Thorgrinn only)
orcus.offer: For one night the iron remembers flesh: warmth, taste, the weight of a cup.
orcus.effect: Thorgrinn experiences full bodily sensation for one night (Hearthwatch or the Night Before the Horns). No mechanical change to his body.
orcus.price: +3 Orcus; disposition becomes claimant. His soul coin glows green whenever Orcus is near, for the rest of the campaign.

vampyr.name: What Is Owed
vampyr.offer: Vampyr shows the web of debts in the mountain as threads of red light.
vampyr.effect: Reveals who owes whom: points straight to E2 (foundry requisitions) and to Dagnner's duplicate of E3.
vampyr.price: +2 Vampyr. The asker takes a Blood-Debt.

vampyr.name: The Bond That Holds
vampyr.offer: A chosen NPC's loyalty is made certain.
vampyr.effect: One NPC (Dagnner, Ketta, a unit of Vanguard soldiers) becomes reliably loyal to one PC for the arc, no check required.
vampyr.price: +3 Vampyr. The NPC is blood-bound: their will erodes while Vampyr is Claiming. If discovered, Civilian Accord −1. Directly opposes Bunch's prophecy.

vampyr.name: Thirst of Iron
vampyr.effect: One weapon deals +1d6 necrotic damage and its wielder regains hit points equal to the necrotic dealt, once per turn, until the end of the arc.
vampyr.price: +2 Vampyr. The wielder takes a Blood-Debt; Vampyr sees through every wound the weapon makes.

vecna.name: The Redacted Line
vecna.offer: Vecna recites the contents of a sealed or destroyed page.
vecna.effect: Gives the full text of one sealed document before it is found (Hadrik's E5, Baldrik's E3, Odran's ledgers). The paper itself must still be found.
vecna.price: +2 Vecna. The asker gives one true secret, written into Vecna's ledger.

vecna.name: A Record Nobody Can Edit
vecna.effect: One authenticated document cannot be destroyed, altered or forged for the rest of the campaign (fits 8.4).
vecna.price: +2 Vecna. The holder gains the Whispered Eye: Vecna may look through their senses for one minute at a moment of the GM's choosing.

vecna.name: The Unwritten Step
vecna.offer: The walls of the mountain become a sentence Vecna can skip.
vecna.effect: Once, the party moves between two places they have seen in Kharad-Varr, ignoring doors, wards, guards and distance (e.g. straight into the Heartworks).
vecna.price: +1 Vecna. Each traveller tells Vecna one true secret they have never knowingly given him.

orcus.beat: At the edge of the last mist a second road runs beside the stone one — black, smooth, unmarked by hammers — for a hundred yards, then ends at a cairn of rusted soul coins. If Thorgrinn accepted the Black Road, it does not end: it runs on towards the hold.
orcus.hook: Edda's death register (1.2) lists Thorgrinn as dead. A voice only Thorgrinn hears: "The register is correct." → Correcting the register and Hearthwatch (3.5b).

vampyr.beat: At the feast, the commission Hadrik offers has a signature line marked to be signed 'in the old way'. Nobody at the table can say what that means. Anyone with a Blood-Debt sees the wine as black.
vampyr.hook: Damien recognises obligation language when he reads it → inspecting and negotiating the commission (1.4) rather than accepting it.

vecna.beat: The courier's message to Kharad-Varr contains one sentence nobody told Edda: a detail from inside the Barovian loop.
vecna.hook: Who reads couriers' dispatches before the generals do? → Venn Slate, the records clerk, and the military archive (3.2–3.4).

orcus.beat: The wounded courier is dying on the floor of the side chamber. Orcus offers, conversationally, to count how many in the broken lift still breathe.
orcus.hook: Accepting tells them seven are alive — and starts a quiet clock. → Urgency for 2.1 and 2.3 without any new enemy.

vampyr.beat: When Thorgrinn touches the two-rivet shield, one rivet weeps a single red drop (only if Vampyr is obsessed with him). It cannot hold the shield: it was given freely.
vampyr.hook: Baldrik says he 'paid for Heddra's roof'. The debt framing is Vampyr's language in Baldrik's mouth. → Pulling at it leads toward his admission (Baldrik event 1).

vecna.beat: One wounded soldier remembers everything about the raid except the order he was given. There is a clean blank where it should be. Vecna offers to fill it.
vecna.hook: The order was the 'support households' clause. → Tovik's dated gauge sheet (E1) and the first hint of R2.

orcus.beat: In Lift Shaft IX the dead workers' tools hang where they fell. If Orcus is Claiming, the first ordinary enemy killed here rises as a husk.
orcus.hook: Naming the dead (Tovik knows them) gives them to Hearthwatch instead of to Orcus. → 3.5b, and Skrik later owning the sabotage.

vampyr.beat: Blood from the fight runs into the poisoned channel and turns black. If Vampyr is Claiming, one 20-foot stretch becomes a Blood Tide zone (difficult terrain; DC 16 Con on entry or 2d8 necrotic).
vampyr.hook: Why is the water already poisoned? → The dead fungal samples and flow markers of R1.

vecna.beat: Urzha's dated well records are missing one torn page. Vecna offers it.
vecna.hook: Refusing and asking Urzha instead earns her respect. → R1 through people rather than shadows; the Urzha–Skrik partnership.

orcus.beat: Runa's calculations include a casualty estimate she could not bring herself to write down. Orcus says the number out loud, in her voice.
orcus.hook: Runa breaks and shows her bypass sheets. → R3 early, through family rather than through the Gift.

vampyr.beat: Baldrik's signature on the classification smells of iron. If Vampyr is a claimant, it glows faintly to anyone carrying a Blood-Debt.
vampyr.hook: → Confronting Baldrik with the signature: his admission (event 1) on the party's terms, not Vampyr's.

vecna.beat: 'Three routes to the same lie' gains a fourth that only Vecna can see. This is the natural place to offer the Redacted Line.
vecna.hook: → E2 and E3; and the cost of knowing first.

orcus.beat: At Hearthwatch, after the last name, Orcus keeps reading. The names he reads are not yet dead: Lowhearth families. Only those at Reaching or higher hear it. If Thorgrinn walked the Black Road, his lantern drifts upstream against the current, like the lantern from below.
orcus.hook: This is the strongest R3 omen in the arc. → Evacuation planning; Heddra's kitchen as the centre of it.

vampyr.beat: At Heddra's table there is one extra place set, and nobody remembers setting it. Vampyr has laid it for whoever it wants back (Finn, Tatyana, Damien's old self).
vampyr.hook: Heddra's hospitality is freely given; Vampyr cannot sit. Saying so aloud ends the omen. → The family conversation 3.5 is built for.

vecna.beat: The Cinder-Tusk invitation arrives under seal. Before anyone breaks it, a PC with the Whispered Eye already knows what it says.
vecna.hook: Do they pretend not to know when Urzha's courier asks? → Trust with the clan, and Chapter 4.

orcus.beat: On the 90-foot Pump Bridge, anyone who falls is caught one foot above the 200-foot drop by something cold. They live. They carry the Death-Mark (Orcus +1).
orcus.hook: → Makes the bridge fight deadly-feeling without being deadlier; the caught PC owes nothing — but Orcus noticed.

vampyr.beat: Korga demands the terms be sealed in blood. If they are, Vampyr Attention +1 and every signatory takes a Blood-Debt to the clan.
vampyr.hook: Offer an object instead: the matched compact copies (E4). → 'A treaty is an object, not a feeling' (4.6).

vecna.beat: The raid was meant to retrieve the clan's copy of the compact. Vecna knows where the dwarven copy is filed, and under what false title.
vecna.hook: → E4 authentication without the archive break-in.

orcus.beat: The 'familiar sentence' is the ritual execution Baldrik once wanted to carry out on desperate thieves. Orcus approves of it, warmly.
orcus.hook: → Baldrik refusing an unlawful order in front of his soldiers (event 2) now means refusing Orcus's applause too.

vampyr.beat: The commission's final clause holds the commissioned's 'body and service' at the council's disposal. Vampyr reads that as ownership — the Sanguine Moon chain all over again. If Finn was freed, he is the one who says it.
vampyr.hook: → Refusing the commission at the public roll, which also breaks any Blood-Debt from 1.4.

vecna.beat: At the public roll Vecna offers to make one name vanish from the record, or appear on it.
vecna.hook: → Honest registration, or a lie that will be found in 8.4.

orcus.beat: In the pump galleries' steam, a horned shape stands where the pressure gauges are. Last Bastion is his harvest bell. If Orcus is Claiming, this is where he offers the Count of the Dying.
orcus.hook: → R3, the controlled inspection, and the turn of the whole arc.

vampyr.beat: Vampyr makes its offer to Baldrik, not to the party: protection for his rank and his family, for a debt. The PCs can see the mark settle on him if they look.
vampyr.hook: → Baldrik submitting evidence and himself to judgement (event 3) is how he breaks it.

vecna.beat: Vecna whispers each general's secret to whoever carries the Whispered Eye: Odran's hidden liability, Brynja's doubt, Hadrik's sealed order.
vecna.hook: → The Stone Council hearing, with the knowledge to aim it.

orcus.beat: At the Vanguard Redoubt the dead the Vanguard made of its own suspected deserters are buried under the parade ground. Their ghosts point at their graves.
orcus.hook: → Evidence of Vanguard brutality that moves Dagnner — she knew two of them.

vampyr.beat: The displaced households owe Korga for protection, exactly as Lowhearth owes Hadrik. Vampyr does not care which side wins; it is fed either way.
vampyr.hook: → Urzha's rejected limited settlement (R4) and a settlement that frees both peoples from protection-debt.

vecna.beat: On the war table's map one route is missing: the narrow service passage to the Heartworks. Vecna offers the Unwritten Step.
vecna.hook: → Skrik can supply the same route honestly.

orcus.beat: As orders are written that send soldiers to hold fronts, a voice counts the ones who will not return.
orcus.hook: → Choosing which front the party takes (7.1) with full knowledge of what it costs elsewhere.

vampyr.beat: Baldrik's 'order he cannot postpone' arrives sealed in red wax that is still warm.
vampyr.hook: → The moment for Baldrik to refuse (event 2) if he has not.

vecna.beat: Vecna offers to tell them which of the three fronts truly matters.
vecna.hook: Accepting reveals the next Siege Dispatch before it is drawn (+1 Vecna). → The war council of 7.1.

all.beat: During the long rest before the horns, each present power visits its marked PC in a dream. This is the last offer before the war. Refusing here at real cost reduces that power's Attention by 1.
all.hook: Run it as one short beat per marked PC, then ring the war horns at dawn.

orcus.beat: On the chosen front, if Orcus is Claiming, fallen raiders rise as husks at the start of round 3. Radiant damage, fire or Legna's ravens deny them.
orcus.hook: → The Upper Gate or Lower Bridge countdown, with something worse than losing ground at stake.

vampyr.beat: Korga falls. Vampyr speaks through his blood: "Give him to me and the war ends tonight." A vampiric Korga is exactly the ninth-session villain this arc refuses to create.
vampyr.hook: Refusing (Vampyr −1) and ending the war by terms is the arc's answer. Bunch's prophecy speaks here if fulfilled.

vecna.beat: The pressure gauge's needle settles on a number that is also a sentence, if you know how to read it.
vecna.hook: → The Heartworks timeline; what the party knows Hadrik knew.

orcus.beat: If Orcus is Arriving, his echo stands at the regulator. Each failed Last Bastion stage gives Orcus +1. If the party wins cleanly, he sets down the scythe: "No harvest. Again." (Orcus −2.)
orcus.hook: → The epilogue: whether Orcus leaves as an enemy, a rival or an admirer.

vampyr.beat: If Baldrik carries a Blood-Debt, it is still on him at the family conversation. A freely chosen act between the brothers — not forgiveness, just a choice — cancels it.
vampyr.hook: → 'Brothers, not a verdict'. The shield offered without terms.

vecna.beat: 'The record nobody gets to edit.' Vecna offers to edit it. Only he could.
vecna.hook: Refusing: Vecna −2, and he is genuinely impressed. Accepting: the record says what they want, and Vecna owns the difference.

all.beat: The next morning each present power leaves a calling card where the PCs will find it. See 'Calling Cards'.
all.hook: → What Hunts Them Next: the campaign after this one.

outcomes.label: Strahd died permanently
outcomes.effect: No Strahd echo. The mists that brought them stay gone; Vistani routes into Ironfist country now run in daylight.
outcomes.hook: Baldrik's Vistani contact (Mirela) can carry letters back to whoever survived Barovia's end.

outcomes.label: Accepted Strahd's Courtesy (the short rest)
outcomes.effect: Guest-Right Remembered. Once in the arc, when a host offers the party hospitality under false pretences (Hadrik's feast counts), a PC may sense it: they learn whether the host intends harm tonight.
outcomes.hook: Strahd's last letter, delivered by a raven a year late, thanking them for 'the hour'.

outcomes.label: Refused Strahd's Courtesy
outcomes.effect: No Hour Given. Once in the arc, the party may refuse an enforced delay (a hearing adjourned, a summons, a wait for permission) and act first; the refusal is legally defensible.
outcomes.hook: None needed: this is a reputation the Ironfists understand.

outcomes.label: Honoured Tatyana's agency
outcomes.effect: Her Own Name (item). Once in the arc, a PC may reroll a failed save against being charmed, commanded or claimed, and say whose choice it is.
outcomes.hook: A letter, signed only 'I.', from somewhere far from Barovia.

outcomes.label: Tatyana's choice was taken
outcomes.effect: No mechanical penalty. Vampyr omens use her voice at least once.
outcomes.hook: Somewhere she is still deciding what she owes them.

outcomes.label: Finn was freed (all three Chains broken)
outcomes.effect: Finn can be present in Kharad-Varr (via Baldrik's Vistani route, arriving at Session 3). He is a halfling vampire who chooses not to feed on the unwilling. Vampyr wants him back: while he is present, Vampyr's beats prefer him.
outcomes.hook: Finn's three chains echo the commission's three clauses (5.1). He recognises them before anyone else.

outcomes.label: Finn was destroyed or remains claimed
outcomes.effect: No Finn. If he was destroyed, Orcus omens use his voice. If he remains claimed (mist), Vampyr does.
outcomes.hook: 'Don't make this weird' written in frost on a window.

outcomes.label: Spared or saved a bride
outcomes.effect: Each bride saved is a creature who owes them nothing and knows it. Volenta, if saved, may write offering service as an oathbreaker seeking a new oath (Legna's material).
outcomes.hook: Ludmilla's Black Sun notes are wanted by Vecna; Anastrasya's mist is wanted by Vampyr.

outcomes.label: Destroyed all three brides
outcomes.effect: Three Ashes. Vampyr cannot lay a Blood-Debt on a PC who struck a bride's final blow unless that PC accepts a Gift first.
outcomes.hook: Nobody in Kharad-Varr believes this story until Dagnner does.

outcomes.label: The Wish came from Damien's djinn
outcomes.effect: The Djinn's Witness (item). The debt is settled. Once, the djinn appears to witness a contract and swear to its terms — a perfect authentication before the Stone Council.
outcomes.hook: The djinn writes once, to complain.

outcomes.label: The Wish came through Vecna (the Borrowed Ending)
outcomes.effect: The Borrowed Ending (item) is live: the agreed price stands (Damien's memory, Vesper's Whispered Eye, Bunch's secret, Legna's first true name, or Thorgrinn's coin inscriptions). Vecna begins at least at Reaching.
outcomes.hook: Every Vecna beat in this arc is also a reminder of the price.

outcomes.label: Arl the pit fiend fought for them under contract
outcomes.effect: Arl's Acknowledgement (item). The contract is closed; the recognition clause stands. An infernal auditor may ask, once, whether Arl aided them. Answering truthfully costs nothing — and is a perfect example of a fair contract to set beside Hadrik's commission.
outcomes.hook: If someone asks why a pit fiend's contract was fairer than their own general's, let it land.

outcomes.label: Thorgrinn walked the Black Road
outcomes.effect: Orcus is a claimant on Thorgrinn specifically and starts at least at Reaching. The Black Road beat in Session 1 continues to the hold.
outcomes.hook: Orcus's offer of restoration to flesh is not trustworthy, and Sister Yrsa will say so.

outcomes.label: Thorgrinn refused the Black Road
outcomes.effect: The Road Back. The keepsake box is the surviving connection. Once in the arc, Thorgrinn has advantage on a check or save made to protect family or to refuse a claim on his body.

outcomes.label: Showed mercy before victory in Vallaki

combined.name: The Undeath Schism
combined.premise: Harvest and Thirst both want Thorgrinn's soul coin: Orcus as a death denied, Vampyr as a covenant refused.
combined.rule: When both are Reaching or higher, their omens interfere. Once per chapter the party can play one against the other: a Gift from one may be refused by invoking the other's claim (no Attention cost, but both +1 at the next threshold check).
combined.turn: Their quarrel gives the party leverage, not safety: the first power to reach Arriving tries to destroy the other's mark on its PC.

combined.name: The Ledger of the Dead
combined.premise: Vecna wants the names Orcus collects. The Hearthwatch register and the corrected death register are their battlefield.
combined.rule: Any document listing the dead (the death register, Hearthwatch names, the missing shift's roster) counts as both 'sealed' for Vecna and 'a harvest' for Orcus. Destroying or falsifying one feeds both (+1 each).
combined.turn: A fair record of the dead, publicly kept, starves both.

combined.name: Blood Remembers
combined.premise: Vampyr's covenants are written; Vecna reads everything written.
combined.rule: A signed Blood-Debt is also a secret Vecna can read: a PC with both marks gives Vecna one free look through their senses per chapter.
combined.turn: The public roll (5.2) and the council record (8.4) can release debts and secrets together.

combined.name: The Council of Broken Gods
combined.premise: All three were freed or angered by the Unkindness. None of them caused this war.
combined.rule: If all three are Reaching or higher, they negotiate with each other through the PCs, offering joint Gifts (combine any two, total Attention cost split as the players choose).
combined.turn: In 8.6 the three calling cards arrive together, and the next campaign is a war over the Unkindness rather than with it.

calling.orcus: A soul coin left on Heddra's step, warm, stamped with a horned skull: an invitation to an audience in the Abyss, or a declaration of war, depending on disposition.
calling.vampyr: A red-sealed letter in Finn's handwriting (or Tatyana's, or Damien's own) that none of them wrote, naming a city and a date.
calling.vecna: A page from the Tome of Strahd that was not in the Tome, describing tomorrow.

reputation: 4+ acts of mercy (spared powers, saved brides, Finn freed, Tatyana honoured, mercy in Vallaki, a Saving Hand)
Civilian Accord starts at 1. Urzha and Sister Yrsa have heard the stories through the Vistani. Hadrik expects to be able to shame them.
No change. The stories contradict each other.
0–1 acts of mercy, several destroyed foes
Defence Readiness starts at 3 and Hadrik starts Supportive: soldiers want heroes like that. Civilian Accord cannot rise above 3 until a public act of mercy in Kharad-Varr.
